title: Pension Accounting Calculations and Journal Entries

step_1_pension_expense: Corridor calculation: Greater of $2,000K or $1,800K = $2,000K × 10% = $200K. Loss $300K > $200K corridor. Amortize excess ($100K) over avg service life (assume 10 years) = $10K.
comprehensive_example.journal_entry:
DR Pension Expense $154K
DR Plan Assets $200K
   CR Cash $200K
   CR Pension Liability $154K

key_relationships: PBO increases: Service cost, interest cost, actuarial losses, prior service cost grants
PBO decreases: Benefits paid, actuarial gains
Plan assets increase: Contributions, actual returns
cpa_exam_tips: Expected return reduces expense, actual return affects assets
Benefits paid reduce BOTH PBO and assets (wash)
Interest cost = Beginning PBO × discount rate
Corridor: 10% × greater of PBO or FV assets

key_points: Pension expense = Service + Interest - Expected return + Amortizations
Benefits paid reduce both PBO and assets
Funded status = Plan assets - PBO (liability if negative)
